words.gram: masculine accusative singular inanimate demonstrative pronoun

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And did you ever think of me?
There were difficult moments in life.

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.

examples.text: Очень хорошо, и к Кате поближе.
examples.trans: Very good, and closer to Katya.

examples.text: Тебя вспомнишь — и уже не так плохо.
examples.trans: One remembers you, and things do not seem so bad.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Мы договорились: ты не вмешиваешься в мою жизнь.
examples.trans: We agreed: you do not interfere in my life.
I need to talk to Katya.
Well, alright, let's make a deal.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вспомнили, что у вас есть дочь?
examples.trans: Did you remember that you have a daughter?

examples.text: Он так бежал, что гостиницу забыл.
examples.trans: He ran so fast that he forgot the hotel.
Victor Petrovich, what happened?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'major' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты же говорил, что ты майор.
examples.trans: You said that you were a major.
This is Major Lavrov.
The major speaks calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.

examples.text: Она ничего об этом не знала.
examples.trans: She knew nothing about it.
He left me this hotel.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Vitya, meet her right now.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.
And where are you going right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Yes, I already know that.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: Tomorrow we have an important event.
He is on an important mission right now.
It's an important question.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'дание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'on a mission' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is on an important mission right now.

examples.text: Вы не знаете, что мы на задании?
examples.trans: Don't you know that we're on a mission?
This is a secret mission.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Mom, hi! I have come back already.
Hi, Dad!
Hi! How are things?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, I already know that.

examples.text: Тебя вспомнишь — и уже не так плохо.
examples.trans: One remembers you, and things do not seem so bad.
Well, there you go, it has started already.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'returned / came back', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: Now I will have to return my wife's fur coat.
I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?
You are under my roof now.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!
examples.trans: I need to step outside for fresh air urgently!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I work right here for you.
Nobody here will touch you.
Nobody is going to fire you here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У неё на новом месте всё в порядке.
examples.trans: Everything is fine with her at the new place.
Chef, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Сейчас попрощаемся, выпьем, и всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, and what do you do for a living?
I work right here for you.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У неё на новом месте всё в порядке.
examples.trans: Everything is fine with her at the new place.

examples.text: У вас здесь всё в порядке?
examples.trans: Is everything alright here with you?
Now let's go through everything in order.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So this is your personal plan?

examples.text: Твоя кухня могла бы спасти положение.
examples.trans: Your cuisine could save the situation.
It was your husband who hired me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'father' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.
He left me this hotel.

examples.text: Моя бывшая жена — хозяйка этого отеля.
examples.trans: My ex-wife is the owner of this hotel.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'мениться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'changed', paired with 'изменяться'.

examples.trans: Nothing has changed here.
You've changed.

examples.text: Узнаёшь? У нас здесь ничего не изменилось.
examples.trans: Recognise it? Nothing has changed here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бедить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'convinced', paired with 'убеждать'.

examples.text: Ты убедила меня взять его на работу.
examples.trans: You convinced me to hire him.
You convinced him?
She convinced me to stay.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.

examples.text: Ты убедила меня взять его на работу.
examples.trans: You convinced me to hire him.
Go and hire Galileo.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I work right here for you.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.
No, I am going back to work.

meanings.en: still, as before, just as previously
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-прежнему').

examples.trans: He still does not care about anyone.

examples.text: От вас я по-прежнему жду участия.
examples.trans: I still expect participation from you.

examples.text: Они по-прежнему живут в этом доме.
examples.trans: They still live in this building.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I still have to inspect the whole hotel.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'плевать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'does not care'.

related.gloss: not to does not care (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: He still does not care about anyone.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наплевать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and does not care on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Катя сегодня уезжает в другой город.
examples.trans: Katya is leaving for another city today.
Thank goodness, we dodged a bullet today!

examples.text: Давай сегодня спокойно, я тебя умоляю.
examples.trans: Let's keep it calm today, I beg you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will fire', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: They just fired me.
Who fired you?
Nobody is going to fire you here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody here will touch you.
No, I am going back to work.

examples.text: Нет, мне ваши деньги не нужны.
examples.trans: No, I do not need your money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.
Do not be afraid, Mom does not bite.
I work as a cook in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы договорились: ты не вмешиваешься в мою жизнь.
examples.trans: We agreed: you do not interfere in my life.

examples.text: Мы же пришли сюда за вами!
examples.trans: We came here following you, after all!

examples.text: А то, что мы с вами переспали...
examples.trans: And the fact that you and I slept together...

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: За что она хотела меня уволить?
examples.trans: Why did she want to fire me?
They wanted to put me to sleep too!
I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.

meanings.en: to communicate, to socialise, to have contact
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to have contact'.

examples.text: Мы хотим с тобой общаться нормально.
examples.trans: We want to talk with you normally.
I am not allowed to talk with you.
We talk often.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: No, it is fine, everything is good.

examples.text: Мы хотим с тобой общаться нормально.
examples.trans: We want to talk with you normally.
Everything's fine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!

examples.text: Моя бывшая жена — хозяйка этого отеля.
examples.trans: My ex-wife is the owner of this hotel.

examples.text: А ещё лучше — из этого города.
examples.trans: And even better, from this city.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: I will be waiting for your return!
Give me just one.
Some water, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You can go stroll around for another five years.

examples.text: А ещё лучше — из этого города.
examples.trans: And even better, from this city.
I still have to inspect the whole hotel.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Get out of my office!

examples.text: Ну я же не вчера родился, а?
examples.trans: Well, I was not born yesterday, huh?

examples.text: А что тут у вас происходит?
examples.trans: And what is going on here with you?

meanings.note: From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.text: Тогда ты дашь ему ещё один шанс.
examples.trans: Then you will give him one more chance.
I've got every chance.
This is your chance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.
Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: So we will see each other often.

examples.text: Никто не видел, где все тележки?
examples.trans: Has anyone seen where all the carts are?

examples.text: А ты Дениса сегодня не видела?
examples.trans: And have you seen Denis today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in no way', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nobody here will touch you.
Then do not be in a hurry.
Nobody is going to fire you here.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: Denis, can you help me, please?
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'звониться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach by phone', paired with 'дозваниваться'.

examples.text: Я никак не могу ему дозвониться.
examples.trans: I cannot reach him by phone at all.

examples.text: Я не могу дозвониться до своей жены.
examples.trans: I cannot get through to my wife.
At home I can't reach him.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, would leave', paired with 'уходить'.

examples.trans: Blow into this tube yourself.
Try our new hot dish!
I want him to leave.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: He left with some lady.
What nonsense.
Some man called you.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'with a lady' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Старый кредит отдам и новый возьму.
examples.trans: I will pay off the old loan and take a new one.

examples.text: Давайте, дамы и господа, наполним бокалы!
examples.trans: Come on, ladies and gentlemen, let's fill our glasses!
He left with some lady.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: У меня где-то универсальный ключ был.
examples.trans: I had a master key somewhere.
He's somewhere here.
I've seen it somewhere.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ниверсальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('universal / master').

examples.text: У меня где-то универсальный ключ был.
examples.trans: I had a master key somewhere.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень универсальный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very universal choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'key' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня где-то универсальный ключ был.
examples.trans: I had a master key somewhere.
Give me the keys.
Where's the key?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: This simply cannot be happening!

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: Я очень хочу быть с Катей.
examples.trans: I really want to be with Katya.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: I will go, bite each other without me.
No, I am going back to work.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Пойдём проверим этот номер прямо сейчас!
examples.trans: Let's go check that room right now!
Check the soldering iron.
We'll check everything right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Denis, this is my mom.
Mom, this is my boyfriend Denis.
Yes, I already know that.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Завтра шеф должен быть на больничном.
examples.trans: Tomorrow the chef must be on sick leave.

examples.text: Что ты в моём номере делаешь?
examples.trans: What are you doing in my room?
Go upstairs to the room right now.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Vitya, meet her right now.
Tell me straight: what do you want?

examples.text: А живую змею в кастрюлю спрятал.
examples.trans: And I hid the live snake in a pot.
